config.name: Great Ocean Walk
config.description: From Apollo Bay along the Otway coast past Cape Otway to the Twelve Apostles, with hike-in campgrounds. Beach sections that depend on the tide are carried as alternates, each named after the nearest numbered decision point.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 1 Storm Point
waypoints.description: Storm Point Decision Point 1: No inland track exists for these short sections of beach walk. Only attempt to walk along the coast during low-tide and calm sea conditions. The beach is occasionally covered by rising tides and waves. Wait for water to recede and determine if it is safe before proceeding.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 1A Storm Point
waypoints.description: Storm Point Decision Point 1A: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland routs. Only attempt to walk along the coast during low-tide and calm sea conditions. The beach and rock platforms for the mext 500m to the west require some rock scrambling and can be frequently covered by rising tides and waves.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 5 Elliot River
waypoints.description: Elliot River Decision Point 5: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland route crossing the river on stepping stones. The coast to Blanket Bay is regularly covered by rising tides and waves and consist of deep gutters, poor sightlines, rock scrambling and lack of escape areas.

waypoints.name: Elliot Ridge Hike-in Campground
waypoints.description: Elliot Ridge Hike-in Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is located on a sheltered ridge top, nestled amongst a tall eucalypt forest. Inhabited by koalas and nocturnal Yellow-bellied Gliders. Facilities include: two untreated rainwater tanks, two composting toilets, a three-sided shelter with camp table and seating, 8 individual hike-in campsites with a limit of 3 people per site. Distance from Apollo Bay Visitor Centre to Elliot Ridge Hike-in Campground is 10km (approx 3hrs 30mins). Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 6 Blanket Bay
waypoints.description: Blanket Bay Decision Point 6: Only attempt the next 200m coastal section during low tide and calm seas conditions. Retrace your steps a short distance to inland Katabanut Track if unsure.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 6A Blanket Bay
waypoints.description: Blanket Bay Decision Point 6A: Take the inland track. The beach and rock platforms here can become reqularly covered by rising tides and ocean waves.

waypoints.name: Blanket Bay Hike-in Campground
waypoints.description: Blanket Bay Hike-in Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is set amongst coastal woodlands, facing east across a sheltered bay, with a waterfall adjacent to the campsite. The dedicated hike-in campground is approximately 50m from the car based campground. Facilities include: an untreated rainwater tanks, a three-sided shelter with camp table and seating, toliets and untreated rainwater available in the nearby car-based campground. 8 individual hike-in campsites with a limit of 3 people per site. Distance from Elliot Ridge Hike-in Campground to Blanket Bay Hike-in Campground is 12km (approx 4hrs 30mins). Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Blanket Bay Campground
waypoints.description: Blanket Bay Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) has sheltered sites near the beach. Access is via Blanket Bay Road turning from Lighthouse Road. Blanket Bay Road is a relatively narrow gravel road and is not suitable for large buses or caravans. Facilities include: communal fireplaces with hotplates and picnic tables, pit toilets and a taps providing limited tank rainwater. Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 6B Blanket Bay
waypoints.description: Blanket Bay Decision Point 6B: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland route. The rock platforms and gutters along the coast to Parker Inlet are impassable due to rising tides and waves.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 7 Parker Inlet river crossing
waypoints.description: Parker Inlet river crossing Decision Point 7: No inland track exists for the next 100m. Wait for water to recede and determine if it is safe before proceeding. The estuary is occassionally covered by rising tides, large ocean wave swells and floodwaters.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 7A Parker Inlet river crossing
waypoints.description: Parker Inlet river crossing Decision Point 7A: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland route. Do not attempt to walk along this coastal section. The beach and rock platforms for the next 2km can be regularly covered by rising tides and waves and consist of deep gutters, poor sightlines, rock scrambling and lack of escape areas.

waypoints.name: Parker Hill Campground
waypoints.description: Parker Hill Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is set on a hill overlooking beach and river. Fires are not permitted at any time. Bring your own drinking water as there is none provided. Sites are unpowered and will accommodate up to six people and one vehicle. Some sites are suitable for campervans or camper trailers. Non-flush toilet provided. Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Cape Otway Lighthouse
waypoints.description: Cape Otway Lighthouse is Australia's most important lighthouse. The Light established in 1848 is perched on towering sea cliffs 90 metres above where Bass Straight and Southern Ocean collide.

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Cape Otway Hike-in Campground
waypoints.description: Cape Otway Hike-in Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is located 600m from the Cape Otway Lighthouse precinct. This site is set amongst coastal woodlands with the Manna Gums attracting regular visits from the local koala population. Facilities include: two untreated rainwater tanks, two composting toilets, a three-sided shelter with camp table and seating. 8 individual hike-in campsites with a limit of 3 people per site. Distance from Blanket Bay Hike-in Campground to Cape Otway Hike-in Campground is 11km (approx 3hrs 45mins). Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Cape Otway Lighthouse Cemetery
waypoints.description: Containing the graves of lightkeeper's families and shipwrecked sailors.

waypoints.name: Rainbow Falls
waypoints.description: Rainbow Falls is a left turn on the beach walking on soft sand, one kilomtre each way. The Falls are actually a colourful spring-fed algae-covered cliff.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 8 Station Beach
waypoints.description: Station Beach Decision Point 8: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland to Aire River. For the next 2km west, Station Beach consists of rock platforms which are regularly covered by rising tides and large waves.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 8A Station Beach
waypoints.description: Station Beach Decision Point 8A: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland routes. The beach and rock platforms for the next 1.5km west to Aire River, and east on Station Beach are regularly covered by rising tides and waves.

waypoints.name: Aire River East Campground
waypoints.description: Aire River East Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is a shady, small spot to camp. It is about half the size of the camping area on the other side of the river (Aire River West). This is a great place for kayaking. The best place to launch is near the bridge at the Aire River campsites. Aire River East has 20 grassy campsites and toilets. Be self-sufficient with drinking water as there is none provided. There are no fireplaces at Aire River East. Bring a portable fuel stoves or gas barbecue. Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Aire River West Campground
waypoints.description: Aire River West Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is a big, flat and open camping area on the western side of the Aire River. It's a good place for large groups to camp. It has 50 grassy campsites suitable for tents and caravans. Toilets and fireplaces provided. Be self-sufficient with drinking water as there is none provided. Enjoy fishing and canoeing on the river. There is a boat ramp nearby. Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Aire River Hike-in Campground
waypoints.description: Aire River Hike-in Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is a sheltered site under a canopy of Beard Heath, set above the Aire River. Facilities include: an untreated rainwater tanks, a three-sided shelter with camp table and seating. Toilets are available in the nearby car-based campground. 8 individual hike-in campsites with a limit of 3 people per site. Distance from Cape Otway Hike-in Campground to Aire River Hike-in Campground is 10km (approx 3hrs 15mins). Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Decision Point 9 Johanna Beach
waypoints.description: Johanna Beach Decision Point 9: No inland track exists for the next 2km. Johanna Beach is occasionally covered by rising tides and ocean waves. Walkers must wade across Johanna River which is occasionally up to 20m wide after heavy rainfalls. To cross, choose shallow, slack water and a solid base before crossing. Wait for waters to recede and determine if it is safe before proceeding.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 9A Johanna Beach
waypoints.description: Johanna Beach Decision Point 9A: Take the inland track. The next access from the beach is 500m west. Only attempt to walk along the coast during low tide and calm sea conditions.

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Johanna Beach Campground
waypoints.description: Johanna Beach Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is nestled among the sand dunes, Johanna Beach is a good spot for camping, caravaning, picknicking and walking. Surfing is also popular here. Dogs are permitted on leads in the campground. Facilities include: composting toilets and a taps providing limited tank rainwater. Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 9B Johanna Beach
waypoints.description: Johanna Beach Decision Point 9B: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland track. There is no coastal access from here to Milanesia Beach as the beaches, rock platforms and gutters are impassable due to rising tides, waves and high cliffs with no escape route.

waypoints.name: Johanna Beach Hike-in Campground
waypoints.description: Johanna Beach Hike-in Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is set amongst Casuarinas and located on a ridge offering spectacular coastal views on one side and rural farm land on the other. Facilities include: two untreated rainwater tanks, composting toilet, a three-sided shelter with camp table and seating. 8 individual hike-in campsites with a limit of 3 people per site. Distance from Aire River Hike-in Campground to Johanna Beach Hike-in Campground is 14km (approx 5hrs 15mins). Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 10 Milanesia Beach
waypoints.description: Milanesia Beach Decision Point 10: No inland track exists for the next 300m. River crossing and beachwalking is required. Only attempt to walk along the coast during low tide and calm sea conditions. Wait for water to recede before proceeding.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 10A Milanesia Beach
waypoints.description: Milanesia Beach Decision Point 10A: Take the inland track. The coastline for the next 750m to the west can be regularly covered by rising tides and waves. There are rocky protrusions, poor sightlines, rock scrambling and a lack of escape areas.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 10B Milanesia Beach
waypoints.description: Milanesia Beach Decision Point 10B: Take the inland track. Do not attempt to walk along this coastal sections to Ryans Den. This coastline is regularly covered by rising tides, waves, poor sightlines, cliffs and a lack of escape routes.

waypoints.name: Ryans Den Hike-in Campground
waypoints.description: Ryans Den Hike-in Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is a remote site set amongst tall eucalypts, with spectacular ocean views, both to Cape Otway in the east and Sub Marine Rock to the west. Facilities include: two untreated rainwater tanks, a composting toilet, a three-sided shelter with camp table and seating. 8 individual hike-in campsites with a limit of 3 people per site. Distance from Johanna Beach Hike-in Campground to Ryans Den Hike-in Campground is 14km (approx 5hrs 15mins). Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 11A Wreck Beach
waypoints.description: Wreck Beach Decision Point 11A: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland route. The beach and rock platforms for the next 1.5km, passing the shipwreck anchors, to Moonlight Beach can be regularly covered by rising tides and waves and consist of high cliffs, poor sightlights rock scrambling and lack of escape areas.

waypoints.name: Devils Kitchen Hike-in Campground
waypoints.description: Devils Kitchen Hike-in Campground (managed by Parks Victoria) is a remote site set amongst coastal woodland with great coastal views. Hiker feedback is that the view from the toilet is magnificent. Facilities include: two untreated rainwater tanks, a composting toilet with a view, a three-sided shelter with camp table and seating. 8 individual hike-in campsites with a limit of 3 people per site. Distance from Ryans Den Hike-in Campground to Devils Kitchen Hike-in Campground is 13km (approx 4hrs 45mins). Advance bookings and payment are required year round see http://www.parkstay.vic.gov.au/

waypoints.name: Water (unreliable)
waypoints.description: Water source, listed as unreliable.

waypoints.name: Decision Point 11B Wreck Beach
waypoints.description: Wreck Beach Decision Point 11B: The Great Ocean Walk follows the inland route. Do not attempt to walk along this coastal section. The beach and rock platforms to the west are impassable due to rising tides and ocean waves, rock scrambling and lack of escape areas.

waypoints.name: Water tap
waypoints.description: Drinking water tap.

waypoints.name: Princetown Campground
waypoints.description: Princetown Recreation Reserve and Campground. Facilities include undercover BBQ area, picnic tables, hot showers, playground, tennis court and laundry. Powered and unpowered sites at very affordable prices. No bookings required.

waypoints.name: Gibson Steps
waypoints.description: Take 86 steps down to the beach below to be dwarfed by the 70-metre high vertical cliffline. Walk along the beach to the enormous offshore rock stacks

waypoints.name: Twelve Apostles
waypoints.description: Created by constant erosion of the limestone cliffs of the mainland beginning 10-20 million years ago, the stormy Southern Ocean and blasting winds gradually eroded the softer limestone, forming caves in the cliffs. The caves eventually became arches and when they collapsed rock stacks up to 45 metres high were left isolated from the shore. View the 12 Apostles at sunrise and sunset as they change colour from dark and foreboding in shadow to brilliant sandy yellow under a full sun.
